facts.value: The first library room was established in the south-west cloister of the cathedral in the 15th century.
facts.quote: the first library room was established, in the south-west cloister of the cathedral, in the 15th century

facts.value: In 1590 the whole library was moved to the Lady Chapel.
facts.quote: In 1590 the whole library was moved to the Lady Chapel

facts.value: The Chained Library, with manuscripts chained to their places, was established in 1611 by Thomas Thornton.
facts.quote: in 1611 the Chained Library (with books in manuscript chained to their places) was established by Thomas Thornton

facts.value: About 229 manuscripts, mainly theological, dated from the 8th to the 16th centuries.
facts.quote: some 229 manuscripts, mainly theological, dated from the 8th to the 16th centuries

facts.value: The Hereford Gospels, in Anglo-Saxon characters, date to around 780 and were the only book to survive the 1055 fire.
facts.quote: Hereford Gospels in Anglo-Saxon characters, dates to around the year 780 and was the only book to survive the 1055 fire

facts.value: The library is described as the only one of its type to survive with all chains, rods and locks intact.
facts.quote: the only library of this type to survive with all of the chains, rods and locks still intact

facts.value: A general survey of chained libraries says only five worldwide survive with their original furniture, chains and books.
facts.quote: Worldwide, only five chained libraries have survived with their original furniture, chains, and books

facts.value: Date of the books differs by source: the Library article says most date to about 1100; the Chained library article says mostly from the 12th century.
facts.quote: Most of the books in the collection date to about 1100

facts.value: A new library building designed by Sir William Whitfield was opened on 3 May 1996 by the Queen.
facts.quote: a new building designed by Sir William Whitfield was opened on 3 May 1996 by the Queen

facts.value: In 1988 the Dean and Chapter proposed the sale of the Mappa Mundi; a donation from Sir Paul Getty followed.
facts.quote: In 1988 the Dean and Chapter proposed the sale of the Mappa Mundi

facts.value: The Hereford Mappa Mundi is called the largest medieval map still known to exist. Dating differs by article: c. 1300 (Mappa Mundi article) or the later 13th century (cathedral article).
facts.quote: the largest medieval map still known to exist
